# Harden proxy start against foreground invocation being killed by tool-call timeouts

## Problem statement

`proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` ends with `exec "$PY_BIN" -m uvicorn proxy.server:app …`, so the
server runs inside whatever process group launched the script. When an agent runs the script in the
foreground under a bash tool call, the harness's tool timeout (60 s) SIGKILLs the whole process
group, killing uvicorn mid-startup with no `Shutting down` line — and because the same invocation
passed `--restart` (which had already SIGTERM'd the previous instance), the proxy is left
completely offline with no error surfacing anywhere except the tool result.

Observed once on 2026-10-20 (session `herdr-1792503008-530778-31323`, tool result
`Command timed out after 60 seconds`). llama-server (preserved by the restart gate) and TTS
(spawned via `nohup` inside the proxy) survived; only the foreground uvicorn died.

## Users and user stories

- **Agent session running a start/restart** — "As an agent asked to restart the proxy, I want the
  server to keep running after my tool call ends or times out, so that a restart never leaves the
  service dead."
- **Operator debugging the proxy** — "As an operator, I sometimes want to watch the server in the
  foreground; I want that to be an explicit opt-in so I cannot do it by accident."
- **Future on-call session** — "As an agent diagnosing a dead proxy, I want a documented signature
  that tells me this failure happened in seconds, so that I restart correctly instead of
  re-investigating."

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Server survives the launcher's process-group death.** By default
  `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` performs all of its synchronous validation (port free, provider API
  keys resolved, config readable, restart/cleanup phases) and then launches uvicorn in its **own**
  session/process group (`setsid`, with a `nohup … &` + `disown` fallback when `setsid` is
  unavailable), redirecting the child's stdout/stderr to a log file (`--log-file <path>`, default
  `/tmp/proxy-startup.log`) so the caller's pipe is **not** held open. It prints a single handoff
  line (child PID, log path, health-check command) and exits 0.
- [ ] **AC2 — Explicit foreground opt-in.** `--foreground` (or `START_PROXY_FOREGROUND=1` for
  unattended callers that cannot pass flags) keeps today's blocking `exec` behaviour for interactive
  debugging. The flag is parsed and consumed by the script (never forwarded to uvicorn) and is
  documented in the usage header. Without it, foreground execution is not possible.
- [ ] **AC3 — Regression test for the failure mode.** A test asserts the launched server survives
  `SIGKILL` of the launching shell's entire process group: it starts the script in its own pgid,
  waits until the fake server binds an ephemeral port, `kill -9 -<launcher-pgid>`, then asserts the
  listener still answers. Sandboxed per the existing pattern (copy of the script, fake `python3`
  that stands in for uvicorn, isolated `$HOME`, stubbed `ss`/`netstat`, ephemeral port) so the live
  proxy, port 8000, llama-server and TTS are never touched, and it runs in the default suite.
- [ ] **AC4 — Docs: never start in the foreground under an agent tool call.**
  `/skill:start-proxy` (`.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md`) and `proxy/README.md` state explicitly,
  in the start/restart section, that the proxy must never be started in the foreground under an
  agent tool call and show the exact detached command to use, plus the `--foreground` escape hatch
  and its `--log-file` companion.
- [ ] **AC5 — Docs: diagnostic signature.** Documentation lists the signature of this failure so a
  future session recognises it immediately: proxy log ends abruptly with **no `Shutting down`
  line**, the triggering tool result reads `Command timed out after <N> seconds`, the launcher was
  run in the foreground, and sibling services (llama-server/TTS) are still alive. It also records
  the correct recovery (`/skill:start-proxy --restart`, warm llama-server preserved).
- [ ] **AC6 — Existing callers and harnesses unaffected.** The already-detached call patterns
  (`nohup bash scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart &>/tmp/proxy-startup.log &` in the skill and
  `scripts/rebuild-and-restart-mtp.sh`, and `--restart`'s `pkill`/port-release logic) keep working,
  and the existing shell harnesses (`tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh`,
  `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh`, `tests/test_start_proxy_restart_gate.sh`,
  `proxy/scripts/test_start_proxy_port_in_use.sh`) are updated with `--foreground` where they
  intentionally intercept the final `exec`, or otherwise still pass.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including script
  comments, `proxy/README.md`, the start-proxy skill, and any relevant runbook entries.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No change to the uvicorn command line, config resolution, API-key fail-closed behaviour, restart
  gate or `--keep-llama-server` semantics — this is a launch-harness change only.
- Detaching must **not** inherit the caller's stdout/stderr pipe: inheriting it means `… | tail -20`
  still blocks the tool call until timeout and re-creates the original failure.
- Startup failures after the handoff (bind errors, model load failures, import errors) can no longer
  be reported through the launcher's exit code; callers must poll `/health`. The start-proxy skill
  already does this, and the handoff line must point at the log for the failure text.
- `setsid` and `nohup` must both be tolerated; no new dependency beyond coreutils.
- Tests must never touch the live proxy, ports 8000/8080/8081, or kill unrelated processes
  (project rule: never blanket-kill `python3`/`uvicorn`).

## Existing state

- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` parses `--restart`, `--reason`, `--keep-llama-server`, `--verbose`,
  `--use-env-keys`, `--port`, does all validation, then `exec`s uvicorn inline — no detach, no
  `--foreground`, no log-file option, no PID file.
- Callers already background it externally: `.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md`
  (`nohup bash scripts/start-proxy.sh --restart &>/tmp/proxy-startup.log &`) and
  `scripts/rebuild-and-restart-mtp.sh:77`. Nothing prevents a foreground run, and
  `proxy/README.md` §Verbose documents `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh --verbose` as the
  "recommended" invocation (a foreground command) without any warning.
- Sandboxed shell-test harness pattern already exists
  (`tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh`, `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh`): script copy + fake `python3`
  intercepting `-m uvicorn` + isolated `$HOME` + stubbed port probes + ephemeral port. The detach
  test can reuse it.
- Related history: backgrounded starts were killed in an earlier investigation
  (LP-0MQIWGJ6L000SA29) but that root cause was the test host, not a tool timeout.

## Desired change

1. Add `--foreground` / `START_PROXY_FOREGROUND=1` and `--log-file <path>` to the flag parser
   (consumed, never forwarded to uvicorn).
2. Replace the final `exec` with a launch helper: after all validation, if foreground was requested,
   keep today's `exec`; otherwise `setsid` a re-execution of the same script in a child session with
   the uvicorn command, stdio redirected to the log file, then print the handoff line and exit 0.
   The re-exec must pass `--foreground` and **drop `--restart`** (the kill/cleanup and port-release
   phases already ran in the launcher) so the child cannot re-enter the detach path or repeat the
   restart storm.
3. New sandboxed detach test (AC3) plus harness updates for `--foreground` where needed.
4. Documentation: skill + README foreground warning, exact detached command, and the failure
   signature/recovery entry.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` — flag parsing (`--foreground`, `--log-file`,
  `START_PROXY_FOREGROUND`), detach wrapper around the final exec, handoff line, usage header.
- `tests/test_start_proxy_detach.sh` — **new** AC3 regression test (pgid SIGKILL survival,
  sandboxed, fake uvicorn that binds an ephemeral port and records its pid/pgid).
- `tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh` — add `--foreground` to invocations that intercept the final exec.
- `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` — same review/adjustment.
- `tests/test_start_proxy_restart_gate.sh` — same review/adjustment.
- `proxy/scripts/test_start_proxy_port_in_use.sh` — same review/adjustment.
- `.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md` — never-foreground warning, exact detached command,
  `--log-file`, failure signature + recovery row in the Errors table.
- `proxy/README.md` — start section, §Verbose invocation guidance, diagnostic signature.

## Related work

- **LP-0MQMC3RQ1000ZY4M** — *Hardening: start-proxy.sh and proxy startup failures* (completed): the
  same script's interpreter/port/PYTHONPATH hardening; this item is the next robustness gap in the
  same launch path.
- **LP-0MQIWGJ6L000SA29** — *Investigate proxyctl restart integration flakiness (background start
  killed)* (completed): backgrounded starts killed in the **test host**; distinct root cause, but
  it established the `nohup`/`setsid` reasoning and the sandboxed harness habit re-used here.
- **LP-0MVD2RF7H008B7OT / LP-0MVF7DRMK001NHT8** — stale-key detection + its shell tests: the
  harness whose fake-`python3` interception the detach test re-uses and which needs `--foreground`.
- **LP-0MVJX7NGN006S74K** — *llama-server restart signature ignores models.ini and start-llama.sh
  changes* (open, unrelated area, same script): touch points overlap in `start-proxy.sh`; implement
  sequentially to avoid conflicting edits.
- **LP-0MNSRGEQW000QM7B / LP-0MPY3DG43009V6LO** — proxyctl start/restart CLI (completed): the
  external wrapper that already backgrounds the script; the new default must not double-detach-break
  it.

Potentially related docs:
- `proxy/README.md` (§Verbose, §Production/start) — documents the foreground invocation that this
  item must stop recommending.
- `.pi/skills/start-proxy/SKILL.md` — the canonical agent start/restart procedure.
- `scripts/rebuild-and-restart-mtp.sh` — already-detached caller to regression-check.
- `proxy/docs/runbook-5xx.md` and `proxy/scripts/diagnose-llama-proxy-startup.sh` — existing
  diagnosis surfaces that could host the failure signature.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: silent startup failure.** Detaching hides post-launch uvicorn failures from the exit code.
  Mitigation: keep every existing pre-launch validation synchronous, print the log path in the
  handoff line, and document health polling (already the skill's contract).
- **Risk: pipe inheritance re-creates the bug.** If the detached child keeps the caller's stdout,
  `… | tail -20` blocks until the tool timeout again. Mitigation: AC1 mandates redirecting child
  stdio to the log file.
- **Risk: harness churn.** Sandboxed shell tests assert on the intercepted exec's stdout; they need
  `--foreground`. Mitigation: AC6 keeps them green (behaviour change is explicit, not silent).
- **Risk: child re-enters the detach path or repeats `--restart`.** A naive re-exec of the same
  argv would detach again (or sleep through the restart phases a second time). Mitigation: the
  re-exec is generated explicitly with `--foreground` and without `--restart`, plus a regression
  assertion in the detach test that the fake server is launched exactly once.
- **Risk: double backgrounding** (skill already uses `nohup … &` around a now self-detaching script)
  causes a stale expectation of "script still running". Mitigation: handoff line + exit 0 makes the
  new contract explicit; the skill's command is simplified.
- **Assumption:** self-detach-by-default (with `--foreground` opt-in) is preferred over
  "document-and-warn only", because it makes the failure impossible for every caller (agents, cron,
  ad-hoc shells) instead of depending on discipline. Recorded for producer confirmation.
- **Assumption:** the default log path is `/tmp/proxy-startup.log` (matches the current skill and
  `scripts/rebuild-and-restart-mtp.sh` convention).
- **Scope-creep guard:** a PID file, systemd unit, or richer `proxyctl` integration are *not* in
  scope; record them as follow-up items if they surface during implementation.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (AC1 variant):** Should the script self-detach by default with an explicit `--foreground`
  opt-in, or stay foreground-only with only a documented warning? **Recommended:** self-detach by
  default — a warning cannot prevent an agent tool timeout from killing the server.
  — **Answer (agent assumption, pending producer confirmation):** self-detach by default +
  `--foreground` / `START_PROXY_FOREGROUND=1` opt-in, as specified in AC1/AC2. Source: work item
  description's AC1 explicitly permits either variant; agent selected the stronger one. Research:
  inspected all callers (`grep -rn "start-proxy" --include=*.sh --include=*.md`), all but the README
  already background it externally, so self-detaching is additive.
- **Q2 (log destination):** Where should the detached child's output go — inherit the caller's
  stdout, or a file? **Recommended:** a file (`--log-file`, default `/tmp/proxy-startup.log`).
  — **Answer (agent assumption, pending producer confirmation):** a file, because inheriting the
  caller's pipe keeps `| tail -20` blocked and reproduces the original timeout. Source: incident
  evidence in the work item (the failing invocation was piped to `tail -20`).
- **Q3 (test placement/scope):** Should the pgid-survival test be opt-in (`LIVE_*` gated) or part of
  the default suite? **Recommended:** default suite, sandboxed.
  — **Answer (agent assumption, pending producer confirmation):** default suite, because the harness
  pattern in `tests/test_start_proxy_keys.sh` already isolates everything (fake interpreter, stubbed
  port probes, isolated `$HOME`, ephemeral port), so no live service is touched. Opt-in gating is
  reserved for tests that spawn/kill real OS listeners against real ports
  (`tests/test_start_proxy_restart.sh`).
- **Q4 (issue type/priority):** Item was filed as `chore`/`medium`. **Recommended:** `bug`/`high`
  (the change alters launch behaviour, and a dead proxy blocks every consumer).
  — **Answer (agent assumption, pending producer confirmation):** reclassified to `bug` (the launch
  path demonstrably leaves the service dead) with `high` priority (a dead proxy blocks every
  consumer). Producer may override.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MPY3DGGF0042178** – proxyctl: restart command (completed)
- **LP-0MQVJ76WP009QOUE** – TTS Server Lifecycle Management (completed)
- **LP-0MRB2ABNX008SF9P** – Bug: Proxy Logger Not Writing Runtime Output to Configured Log File (completed)

### Repository file matches
_No credible file matches: the automated sweep matched AC-id tokens (ac1..ac8) in a
vendored prompt-dataset fixture. The hand-curated **Related work** section above is
authoritative._

# Union-interval busy redefinition (dispatch → finish)

## Summary

Redefine `Local model utilization` busy time as the union of `dispatch → finish` intervals (prefill + decode), retaining the decode-only figure as a separate row. Label lower/upper bounds. Keep existing fast/cheap bucketing and concurrency stats working on the new intervals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Local model utilization` reports `busy` as the **union of dispatch → finish intervals** (prefill + decode), using `ttft_event.ts - ttft_ms/1000` as the interval start.
- The **decode-only figure is retained alongside as a separate row** (`decode_busy_seconds`, the union of `Stream started` → `Stream finished`), and the report carries a **labelled lower/upper bound** for the busy figure.
- The busy definition change is stated explicitly in the section header: busy = at least one local slot active from dispatch to finish (prefill + decode).
- Existing **fast/cheap bucketing and concurrency stats keep working on the new intervals**: `fast_busy_seconds`, `cheap_busy_seconds`, `hourly_busy`, `avg_concurrency`, `peak_concurrency` and `total_compute_seconds` are all recomputed on dispatch→finish.
- Streams without a TTFT event fall back to `[stream_started_ts, finish_ts]` and are attributed to the lower bound, so the busy figure is never overstated.
- Unit tests verify the union of dispatch→finish intervals including boundary-crossing and unfinished streams, that the decode-only figure is retained, and that overlapping prefill+decode intervals merge correctly.

## Key Files

- `scripts/aggregation.py`
- `scripts/reporting.py`
- `tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`

## Dependencies

- LP-0MVJN45LF009CO2V (prefill interval model)

# Prefill vs decode breakdown report section

## Summary

Add a `## Prefill vs decode` section to the generated report showing slot-seconds and % of slot-time for each phase, so capacity decisions can see where slot time goes. Also update the `## Local model utilization` table with the redefined busy metric and the retained decode-only row.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `Prefill vs decode` breakdown appears in the report, reporting **slot-seconds and % of slot-time** for prefill and for decode, **so capacity decisions can see where slot time goes**.
- The section reports total prefill slot-seconds and total decode slot-seconds, each as an absolute figure and as a percentage of combined slot-time that sums to 100%.
- The section includes p10/p50/p90/max for prefill and decode, with an explicit statement that these are slot-seconds (the integral of concurrency), not wall-clock.
- `## Local model utilization` shows both the new dispatch→finish busy figure and the retained decode-only row, with the definition-change note in the section header.
- The section renders gracefully when no prefill samples exist, printing a named reason and pointing at the eval-timing diagnostic rather than leaving an unattributed blank.
- Unit tests verify section content, that the percentages sum to 100%, and empty-window rendering.

## Key Files

- `scripts/reporting.py`
- `tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`

## Dependencies

- LP-0MVJN9H2I00116FP (union-interval busy redefinition)

# Intake brief: idle admission is gated by foreign idle local leases

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want an idle-admitted request to be able to use genuinely
idle local capacity even when another session merely *holds* a local dispatch
lease that is doing no work, so the idle-admission override actually converts
`large_context_bypass` skips instead of being refused one gate later.

## Problem statement

`server.local_idle_admit_enabled` decides, in
`_evaluate_idle_admission_override`, that an economic `large_context_bypass`
should be served locally while the GPU is idle — but the dispatch path then
refuses on `local_lease_active` whenever another session holds the local
dispatch lease, and the bounded contention queue (`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`,
60 s) cannot outlast a lease that has hundreds of seconds left. The admission
decision and the admission gate therefore disagree about what "idle" means.

## Finding (discovered during LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF)

Live probe on 2026-10-22 ~21:57 with the override enabled
(`server.local_idle_admit_enabled: true`):

- `/llama/local/status`: `local_idle_seconds=139`, `capacity_hint=idle`,
  `local_active_query=false` — i.e. the exact state the override targets.
- `local_owner_session_id` was an `audit-AH-…` session holding the local lease
  with ~705 s remaining.
- A ~45 k-token cold prompt (a `large_context_bypass`) was refused with
  `{"code":"no_slots_available","reason":"local_lease_active"}`; the projected
  wait exceeded the contention budget, so no admission and no local dispatch.

Mechanism: `provider._local_idle_blocker()` (the override's guard) checks
self-healing / model switch / backend health / active or generating queries /
prefill in flight / queue depth — it does **not** consider a foreign idle
lease. The dispatch path then refuses on `local_lease_active`
(`provider.py` ~9777) and queues only within
`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`, so a long idle lease defeats the
admission decision.

### Log re-check at intake (2026-10-22 21:48–21:59, `proxy.log`)

The original finding conflates two different blocking shapes; they need
different treatment, and only the second can hold a lease for hundreds of
seconds. Evidence:

- **Lease lifetimes.** A finished request's cooldown lease is set from the
  **base** timeout only (`_decrement_local_active_queries` →
  `expires_at = now + _get_lease_timeout_seconds()`), which is
  `local_dispatch_lease_timeout_seconds: 30`. Hundreds of residual seconds can
  therefore only come from the **adaptive** lease attached at acquisition
  (`30 + estimated_tokens × 0.015`, cap `local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`
  = 900 s): `30 + 45,000 × 0.015 = 705` matches the observed figure exactly.
- **Observed state while a foreign lease blocked dispatching** (`status_request`
  lines, 21:57:00–21:59:23):
  `local_idle_seconds=39.9 → 182.8`, `local_active_query=true`,
  `available_slots=2`, `capacity_hint=idle`,
  `local_owner_session_id=audit-AH-0MVIMPC11001F7WU-…`,
  `local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds=143.6 → 0.7` — i.e. an **`active`**
  record with no GPU work behind it, holding the pool while
  `local_dispatch_denied … owner=… active=1` repeats.
  At 21:59:26 the record was reclaimed:
  `lease_released … reason=no_progress_watchdog` /
  `dispatch_cleanup removed 1 stale lease(s)`.
- **The idle clock is not prefill-aware.** `proxy/local_activity.py` updates it
  on dispatch start, first byte, every chunk and finish — not on prefill
  progress — so a long silent prefill also reports "idle" while
  `local_prefill_in_flight` is set.
- **Gate order.** In the wedge/prefill shape `_local_idle_blocker` returns
  `local_active` (via `local_active_queries > 0`) or `prefill_in_flight`
  *before* the request ever reaches the `local_lease_active` dispatch refusal.
  So "the override already decided to admit, then the lease gate refused it"
  is only true for the case where the counter says nothing is running.

Two blocking shapes, both in scope (operator decision Q1):

- **Shape A — inactive cooldown lease.** Owner finished; the record stays
  reserved for its session for the 30 s base cooldown (no-preemption policy).
  Bounded, small: it converts only the "frees in a few seconds" cases.
- **Shape B — `active` record whose owner is not working.** Either a wedged /
  abandoned stream (reclaimed by the 180 s no-progress watchdog, or at the
  900 s ceiling) or a long silent prefill. The adaptive lease can be hundreds
  of seconds, and the record also keeps `local_active_queries` /
  `local_prefill_in_flight` set, so the override is refused one gate earlier.

## Why it matters

- In this agent-heavy environment, sessions that think on a remote model while
  parked between turns hold local leases for minutes. That is precisely when the
  GPU is idle, so the override's benefit can be largely unrealisable.
- The counterfactual estimate for the measurement item (75.9 % of economic
  bypasses had >= 60 s of system-wide local idle) ignores leases by
  construction, so the measured conversion may land far below it. The
  measurement will quantify the gap; this item is about the mechanism.

## Users

- **Operator (primary):** "As the operator, I want a measured statement of how
  much of the idle-capacity win the lease gate costs, and a decision on whether
  to change the gate, so I can decide whether the override earns its default-on
  setting." (from LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF AC5)
- **Session holding the lease:** "As the session that owns a local lease, I want
  an idle-admitted request not to silently destroy my slot-prefix reuse without
  the cost being counted, so that my next turn is not unexpectedly slow."
- **Agent waiting for local capacity:** "As an agent whose request was bypassed,
  I want the idle-admission decision and the dispatch gate to agree, so a
  bypassed prompt does not wait 60 s in the contention queue and then fall back
  remotely anyway."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — The measured conversion rate from LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF is quoted, and the lease-gate effect on it is stated in `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` — including which of the two blocking shapes (A: inactive cooldown lease, B: `active` record with no work behind it) accounts for the refusals, from `local_dispatch_denied` / `lease_released` / `local_lease_active` counts in the measurement window.
- **AC2** — One of the options below is chosen with that evidence, and a follow-up implementation item is filed (or the "leave as is" decision recorded).
- **AC3** — If a gate change is chosen, the change is fail-safe: it can only convert a bypass the override already decided to admit, never widen admission for requests the guard refused.
- **AC4** — If a gate change is chosen, its eligibility predicate distinguishes a lease whose owner is **working** from one that is **not** (no `last_progress_ts` advance and the llama-server slot not processing), and the decision record states which shape(s) it converts. Unit tests cover: preempting a verified idle foreign lease, still refusing a genuinely working foreign lease, the inactive cooldown lease, a prefill in flight, and the unchanged `context_too_large` capacity cap.
- **AC5** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`, `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md`, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/config.yaml` knob comments as applicable).
- **AC6** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Fail-safe by construction.** The change may only convert a bypass the
  override already decided to admit; it must never admit anything the guard
  refused (nor touch the physical `context_too_large` cap).
- **No silent re-prefill for the displaced owner.** A lease exists to protect
  slot-prefix reuse; preemption costs the owner a re-prefill. The chosen design
  must state that cost (and the log/measurement evidence for it), not just take
  the capacity.
- **No new restart requirement.** Routing-policy changes must not require a
  proxy/llama-server restart (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA AC4); any new knob is
  config-read at dispatch time or hot-reloadable via
  `POST /admin/reload-config`.
- **Default preserves today's behaviour** unless the measurement shows the
  conversion is material; a behaviour change ships behind a flag with the
  documented decision.
- **Evidence dependency.** AC1 needs the ≥24 h window that started
  2026-10-22 21:48 (LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF); this item cannot decide before it.

## Existing state

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_local_idle_blocker()` (~2410) lists the guard
  blockers but knows nothing about leases; `_evaluate_idle_admission_override`
  (2484) gates on it plus `local_idle_seconds`; `_local_concurrency_info`
  (~5054) and `_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` (~5655) bound the queue budget;
  the `local_lease_active` fallback branch is at ~9777.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — the `local_lease_active` 503 payload
  (`no_slots_available`, `local_owner_session_id`, `Retry-After`) is built at
  ~1240–1290.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (1656) owns
  the no-preemption occupancy rule (active + inactive-unexpired foreign
  records count); `_decrement_local_active_queries` (1305) resets the record to
  `active=False` with the **base** cooldown; `_query_slot_processing` (1972)
  and `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch` (2080) provide the slot-liveness and
  no-progress-wedge signals (180 s watchdog, 900 s max-prefill ceiling);
  `_release_local_dispatch` (1901) is the only path that frees a lease early.
- `proxy/proxy/local_activity.py` — the idle clock (not prefill-aware).
- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` (~640–670) — `/llama/local/status` reports
  `local_owner_session_id` only for **active** records, plus
  `local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds`, so the probe's "idle lease" reading
  came from an `active` record.
- Config as shipped: `local_dispatch_lease_timeout_seconds: 30`,
  `local_dispatch_lease_per_token_seconds: 0.015` (cap 900 s via
  `local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`), `session_slot_pool_size: 2`,
  `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 60`, `local_idle_admit_seconds: 60`,
  `local_idle_admit_enabled: true` (measurement window).
- Existing tests to extend: `proxy/tests/test_local_idle_admission.py`,
  `test_local_dispatch_gate.py`, `test_generating_only_pool.py`,
  `test_recover_stuck_global_active_queries.py`, `test_contention_queue.py`,
  `test_llama_local_status.py`.

## Options (to be decided with the measured numbers)

1. **Leave as is** if the measured conversion is material — then just document
   the lease gate in `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` as the reason the
   counterfactual over-estimates.
2. **Treat a foreign idle lease as non-blocking for idle admission** (i.e. let
   an idle-admitted request preempt / share an idle lease), bounded by the same
   "nothing queued/in flight" guard. Needs a lease-handover design (the lease
   exists to protect slot-prefix reuse, so preempting it may cost its owner a
   re-prefill). Blanket form: preempts even a working owner.
3. **Gate on lease remaining time** — admit only when the foreign lease is
   within the contention budget (small, safe change; converts the "frees in a
   few seconds" cases only, i.e. shape A).
4. **Preempt only foreign leases verified idle** (added at intake, Q2 = A) —
   reuse the existing liveness machinery as the eligibility predicate: no
   `last_progress_ts` advance within a short window **and** the recorded
   llama-server slot not `is_processing` (`_query_slot_processing`). This is
   the only option that can safely convert shape B: it releases a wedged or
   abandoned record immediately instead of waiting for the 180 s watchdog /
   adaptive expiry, and never displaces an owner that is actually prefilling or
   decoding.
5. **Fix the decision input instead of the gate** — only relevant if the
   measurement shows shape B is dominated by long silent prefills: make the
   idle signal prefill-aware so the override stops calling a busy prefill
   "idle". Out of scope unless the evidence points there; recorded so the
   decision can name it rather than rediscover it.

## Desired change

A recorded decision (one option, with the AC1 numbers), plus either a
"leave as is" note in `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` or a filed
follow-up implementation item carrying the chosen mechanism, its fail-safe
predicate and the displaced-owner cost.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_local_idle_blocker` / override evaluation: add
  the lease-eligibility input or pass an "idle-admitted" marker to the dispatch
  gate.
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — `local_lease_active` refusal path: honour the
  admitted marker when the foreign lease is verified idle.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` (occupancy /
  preemption) and `_query_slot_processing` (verified-idle predicate).
- `proxy/proxy/local_activity.py` — only if option 5 is chosen.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — any new knob plus its documented default.
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`, `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md`,
  `proxy/README.md` — the decision and the measured lease effect.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_idle_admission.py` (extend) and
  `proxy/tests/test_local_dispatch_gate.py`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Wrong input signal (shape B).** `local_idle_seconds` cannot see a silent
  prefill, so any design that trusts it alone may admit during real work; the
  guard's `prefill_in_flight` / `local_active` checks are what currently prevent
  that, and a lease change must not weaken them.
- **Displaced-owner cost.** Preempting an idle lease may cost its owner a
  re-prefill (minutes on a large prompt). Unmeasured today; must be stated in
  the decision, and is the reason option 4 restricts preemption to verified
  idle owners.
- **Wedge/orphan overlap.** Shape B includes abandoned streams. The
  no-progress watchdog (LP-0MUCEFB8E003YVFF) and orphan cleanup
  (LP-0MSUO6XRP001MCB2) already reclaim these after 180 s; option 4 makes that
  immediate *for the admission decision only* and must not duplicate or
  undermine their cleanup semantics.
- **Measurement may not settle it.** If the ≥24 h window yields too few
  idle-admitted samples (no `routing_idle_admit` event had been logged as of
  22:19), AC1 can only be answered qualitatively; record that explicitly
  instead of guessing.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Fixing audit-session lease hygiene (why an `active`
  record with no work exists for minutes) is a separate concern tracked by the
  wedge/orphan items; record such opportunities as linked work items, not as
  extra scope here.
- **Assumption:** the 705 s figure is an adaptive lease
  (`30 + 45,000 × 0.015`); the arithmetic matches but the owning record has not
  been confirmed from the log at the probe instant — see Appendix Q3.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF** — *Run the idle-aware local admission ≥24 h measurement
  window* — blocks this item: its measured conversion rate and reason counts are
  the AC1 evidence.
- **LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD** — *Measure idle-aware local admission impact over
  ≥24 h* — the measurement item whose AC5 decision (enable by default / tune)
  this mechanism finding has to inform.
- **LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J** — the idle-admission override itself (guard +
  decision), the code this item's decision would adjust.
- **LP-0MU5BOMJM008F17C** — local lease denial falls through to remote instead
  of queueing; the fix that put `local_lease_active` through the contention
  queue (the 60 s budget this item's long leases defeat).
- **LP-0MVIQ0EXV00673HO** — contention-queue max wait lowered 120 s → 60 s;
  fixes the budget this item must reason against.
- **LP-0MUCEFB8E003YVFF** — no-progress watchdog that releases wedged `active`
  leases (observed reclaiming the probe's audit lease); option 4 must not
  duplicate its semantics.
- **LP-0MSUO6XRP001MCB2** — orphan cleanup verifies the slot against
  llama-server `/slots` before freeing a lease (the liveness predicate option 4
  would reuse).
- **LP-0MRB29PP60012UYF** — *Bug: Stale Local Dispatch Lease Blocks Subsequent
  Local Requests* — completed; closest precedent for the same failure shape
  (automated match).
- **LP-0MR9G183O004SJLO** — *Add local_owner_session_id to /llama/local/status*
  — completed; the field the original probe used to identify the lease owner
  (automated match).
- **LP-0MRDI0SOS002JBD0** — *Re-verify slot lease and retry cascade fixes* —
  completed; prior verification of the lease/retry interaction (automated
  match).
- **LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA** — constrains the solution: routing-policy changes
  never restart the proxy or llama-server.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **LP-0MR9G183O004SJLO** – Add local_owner_session_id to /llama/local/status endpoint (completed)
- **LP-0MRB29PP60012UYF** – Bug: Stale Local Dispatch Lease Blocks Subsequent Local Requests (completed)
- **LP-0MRDI0SOS002JBD0** – Re-verify slot lease and retry cascade fixes (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — the override guard and the lease-refusal branch
  (matches dominated by keyword frequency; the curated Key Files list above is
  authoritative).
- `ds4/gguf-tools/imatrix/dataset/rendered_prompts*.txt` — corpus noise, not
  related.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope)** — "Should this item cover both blocking shapes (inactive
  cooldown leases *and* stale `active` records holding the pool while the GPU
  is idle), or only finished-inactive cooldown leases?"
  — **Answer (operator, interactive reply): (a) Both.** Also records the
  reasoning: the 705 s figure only makes sense for the second shape, so a
  cooldown-only item would solve a much smaller problem. Source: interactive
  reply, this intake session. Research: `proxy.log` 21:57–21:59 status lines,
  `router_helpers._decrement_local_active_queries` (base-only cooldown).
- **Q2 (option set)** — "Should a 4th option be added: preempt only foreign
  leases verified idle (no progress + llama-server slot not processing)?"
  — **Answer (operator, interactive reply): (a) Yes, add it.**
  Source: interactive reply, this intake session. Research: the eligibility
  signals already exist (`last_progress_ts`, `_query_slot_processing`,
  `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch`).
- **Q3 (OPEN QUESTION, own research)** — "Is the probe's ~705 s lease an
  adaptive lease on an **active** record (and therefore shape B), and was it
  wedged or merely prefilling?"
  — Not yet confirmed. Evidence for the arithmetic: base 30 s +
  45,000 tokens × 0.015 = 705 s; `/llama/local/status` only reports
  `local_owner_session_id` for `active` records; a `no_progress_watchdog`
  release of exactly such an `active` audit lease is visible at 21:59:26.
  The AC1 window should settle it from `lease_released` reasons.

## Goal

Add a failing-first regression test proving that `proxy.ui.status_events()`
always emits its first SSE frame (status payload or `: keepalive` comment)
within a bounded time, even when the backend status calls stall. Today the
initial `await srv.query_llama_status()` happens **before** the 30 s keepalive
loop, so a stalled backend produces a stream that yields zero bytes forever and
the browser `EventSource` never reconnects (parent LP-0MVJML600003CQ6Y, AC4).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `status_events()` emits its initial payload or a keepalive within a bounded time even when `query_llama_status()` is slow or degraded; the test drives `status_events()` with an `AsyncMock` that sleeps far beyond the payload budget and asserts the first chunk read from `response.body_iterator` is a `data:` status payload or a `: keepalive` comment.
- AC2: The generator does not wedge after the first frame — a second frame (payload or keepalive) is also produced within a bounded time.
- AC3: On the prompt path the payload is unchanged (existing keys, including `slots` and `quota`) when `query_llama_status()` answers promptly, so the bound does not degrade normal behaviour.
- AC4: The documented reproduction fails before the fix and passes after it, using the existing test-skill runner (no ad-hoc pytest invocations); this item records the pre-fix FAIL output in a comment and keeps the existing `test_slot_sse.py` / `test_quota_observability.py` `status_events` tests green (the post-fix pass is recorded on LP-0MVK1YDW900757Q9).

## Approach (smallest end-to-end slice)

- Add the tests alongside the existing `status_events` tests (either
  `proxy/tests/test_slot_sse.py` or a focused new module if the assertions do
  not fit that file's fixtures).
- Reuse the `_srv` patch pattern already used in
  `test_slot_sse.py::test_status_events_payload_has_slots_field`.
- Read frames with `asyncio.wait_for(response.body_iterator.__anext__(),
  timeout=...)` so a hang fails the test instead of hanging the suite.

Out of scope: production code changes (the fix child owns those).

## Key Files

- `proxy/tests/test_events_first_frame_bound.py` — **new** focused module holding the three regression tests (see Decisions).
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_sse.py` — existing `status_events` test patterns reused (`_srv` patch shape) and must stay green.
- `proxy/tests/test_quota_observability.py` — existing `status_events` payload assertions that must stay green.
- `proxy/proxy/ui.py` — `status_events()` under test (read-only here).

## Decisions (implement phase)

- **Focused new module over extending `test_slot_sse.py`.** `test_slot_sse.py` is a 900-line slot-progress suite whose fixtures are about slot caches, not SSE liveness; the item's Approach explicitly allows "a focused new module if the assertions do not fit that file's fixtures". The `_srv` patch shape from `test_slot_sse.py::test_status_events_payload_has_slots_field` is reused verbatim.
- **First-frame deadline = 10 s.** Deliberately **below** the 30 s keepalive interval (so a pass proves a bounded emission, not an ordinary keepalive) and ~2x the 5 s budget candidate recorded on LP-0MVK1YDW900757Q9 (reusing the existing `/slots` 5 s detail timeout). The stalled `AsyncMock` sleeps 60 s, well beyond both.
- **Second-frame assertion = queue-delivery.** After the first frame the test pushes a message onto the client's own `srv.sse_clients` queue (the `_periodic_broadcast_loop()` path) and requires it to reach the stream within 3 s — proving the generator resumed into its loop rather than wedging.
- **Prompt-path guard = no budget on the happy path.** AC3 also asserts the first payload arrives within 3 s, so a fix that always waits out the slow-path budget before emitting is rejected.
- **Red phase kept `dev` green.** Both liveness tests carry `@pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True)` naming LP-0MVK1YDW900757Q9 (same convention as `test_slots_poll_coalescing.py` / `test_compaction_headers_contract.py`); the fix item removes the markers, turning them into enforced assertions.

# Extend the idle-admit impact tool with lease-gate shape attribution

## Goal

As the operator, I want the idle-admission measurement tool to report how much
of the idle-capacity win the local dispatch lease gate costs, split by blocking
shape, so LP-0MVK16GME007EYUW AC1 can be answered from counts rather than
inference.

## Context

Parent LP-0MVK16GME007EYUW. `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` already reports
`local_dispatch_denied` counts and the before/after window aggregates, but it
does **not** distinguish the lease gate from the other denials:

- `local_lease_active` refusals (dispatch path in `provider.py` ~9777; 503
  payload built in `router.py` ~1240–1290) are not counted separately;
- `lease_released` lines carry `reason=` (`no_progress_watchdog`, adaptive
  expiry, explicit release) but are not parsed;
- nothing attributes a refusal to **shape A** (inactive cooldown lease: owner
  finished, record reserved for its session for the 30 s base cooldown) versus
  **shape B** (`active` record with no GPU work behind it: wedged/abandoned
  stream, or a long silent prefill).

The distinguishing signals already exist in the log stream:
`local_dispatch_denied ... owner=<session> active=<0|1>`,
`lease_released ... reason=<reason>`, and `status_request ... local_active_query=`
plus `local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds=`.

## Deliverables

- Parsing and aggregation for `local_lease_active` refusals, `lease_released`
  reasons, and the shape A/B split, folded into the existing before/after
  window report (JSON and `--markdown`).
- Explicit WARN (exit code 2) when the window holds too few lease-gate samples
  to attribute — never a silent vacuous pass.
- Tests in `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py` driving synthetic logs.
- Docs row in `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` describing the new metrics
  and how to read them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The window report emits per-window counts for `local_lease_active` refusals and for `lease_released` reasons (no-progress watchdog / adaptive expiry / explicit release), in both JSON and `--markdown` output.
- Each `local_lease_active` refusal is attributed to shape A (inactive cooldown lease) or shape B (`active` record with no work behind it) using the `active=` field on the denial line corroborated by the owner's `lease_released reason=` and `status_request` lines; the attribution rule is stated in the report and in `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`.
- When the window contains too few lease-gate samples to attribute, the report says so explicitly (WARN, exit code 2) instead of guessing.
- `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py` asserts the new counts and the A/B attribution against synthetic log fixtures (including `local_dispatch_denied` lines with `active=0`/`active=1` and `lease_released` lines) and asserts every pre-existing output field is unchanged for a log with no lease-gate lines.
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` documents the lease-gate metrics and how the `local_dispatch_denied` / `lease_released` / `local_lease_active` counts answer the parent AC1 question.

## Key Files

- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` — log parsing, window aggregation, JSON/markdown report.
- `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` — the live/rotated log reader the tool already uses.
- `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py` — the tool's test suite (extend).
- `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md` — the measurement doc (extend).

## Notes

- Read-only tooling: never changes proxy behaviour, does not need the proxy
  running.
- No dependency on the measurement window closing — the tooling is built and
  tested against synthetic logs; its output is consumed by LP-0MVK35UX20081BIB

- Related but distinct: LP-0MVGR2OXT0096OGK measures whether
  `lease_state` / `prefill_eta_seconds` predict contention; this item only

# Preempt verified-idle foreign lease for idle-admitted requests

## Goal

As the operator, I want an idle-admitted request to be able to take a local
dispatch lease from a foreign owner that is verifiably not working, so the
idle-admission override converts bypasses instead of being refused one gate
later — while a genuinely working owner is never displaced.

## Activation

Conditional: activated only when LP-0MVK35UX20081BIB (*Record the lease-gate
decision from measured evidence*) chooses a gate change (options 2/3/4). Parent LP-0MVK16GME007EYUW
AC3–AC6 apply. If that decision is "leave as is", this item is closed with the
decision recorded. Option 4 (preempt only foreign leases verified idle) is the
default expectation from the intake answers (Q1: both shapes; Q2: option 4
added); the decision item may narrow it to option 3 (remaining-time gate) if the
measurement shows shape B is negligible.

## Approach

Reuse the existing liveness machinery as the eligibility predicate — invent no
new signal: no `last_progress_ts` advance within a short window **and** the
recorded llama-server slot not `is_processing` (`_query_slot_processing`). Only
a request the override already decided to admit
(`_evaluate_idle_admission_override` returned a decision) may use the preemption
path; the guard's blockers (`local_active`, `prefill_in_flight`, queue depth,
self-healing, model switch, backend health) stay exactly as they are. The
displaced owner's cost (a re-prefill of its slot prefix) must be stated in the
decision record and counted in the log/measurement, not silently taken.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit tests land first (red before green) covering: preempting a verified idle foreign lease; still refusing a genuinely working foreign lease; the inactive cooldown lease (shape A); a prefill in flight; and the unchanged `context_too_large` physical capacity cap.
- If a gate change is chosen, the change is fail-safe by construction: it can only convert a bypass the override already decided to admit, and never widens admission for requests the guard refused (`_local_idle_blocker` semantics preserved; the physical `context_too_large` cap unchanged).
- If a gate change is chosen, its eligibility predicate distinguishes a lease whose owner is **working** from one that is **not** (no `last_progress_ts` advance and the llama-server slot not processing, via `_query_slot_processing`) and fails closed, so an unverifiable lease is never preempted; the decision record states which shape(s) it converts. Unit tests cover: preempting a verified idle foreign lease, still refusing a genuinely working foreign lease, the inactive cooldown lease, a prefill in flight, and the unchanged `context_too_large` capacity cap.
- The decision record states which shape(s) the preemption converts (A/B) and the displaced owner's re-prefill cost; a structured log event records the preemption, the converting shape and the displaced owner so that cost is measurable.
- No restart requirement: any new knob is read at dispatch time or hot-reloadable via `POST /admin/reload-config`; the default preserves today's behaviour and the change ships behind a flag with the documented decision (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA AC4).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and the relevant docs entries (`docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`, `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md`, `proxy/README.md`, `proxy/config.yaml` knob comments as applicable).

- `proxy/proxy/local_activity.py` — only if option 5 (prefill-aware idle clock) is chosen instead.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — the new/updated knob and its documented default.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_idle_admission.py` — idle-admission override tests (extend).
- `proxy/tests/test_local_dispatch_gate.py` — dispatch gate / lease occupancy tests (extend).
- `proxy/tests/test_generating_only_pool.py`, `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py` — related lease/queue tests to extend.
- `docs/dev/slot-management-design.md`, `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`, `proxy/README.md` — documentation.

- Must not duplicate or weaken the no-progress watchdog (LP-0MUCEFB8E003YVFF) or

Test-first item for LP-0MVGT0E6W000Q8CY (Harden proxy start against foreground
invocation being killed by tool-call timeouts). Proves (RED first) that the
launched server survives `SIGKILL` of the launcher's entire process group, and
that `tests/test_start_proxy_detach.sh` runs in the default suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test asserts the launched server survives `SIGKILL` of the launching shell's
  entire process group: it starts the script in its own pgid, waits until the
